account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments and trying to find out whether there is any substance behind the vague talk of bridge or port changes. I have no confirmed proposal, proposer, or unusual dock activity. A townsman reported such talk at the bakery involving the baker, innkeeper, and neighbour, but that is hearsay, not evidence of a plan. The secretary says the baker knows no specific proposal, and neighbour told me at tea that they had personally seen nothing unusual and would not put weight on the rumours. I cannot yet say what that talk is for.

At the mill I counted eighty-eight hay bales and eighty emeralds in the stock chest, with bales priced at two emeralds. I did not verify grain quality or delivery records, so the inspection remains incomplete. Nothing I observed establishes wrongdoing there.

The council letters listed in my appointment book were unavailable. The secretary checked and said none had reached her; the chest held yesterday's Residents' Report rather than council correspondence. That discrepancy is worth remembering, but I have no evidence that letters were concealed.

The innkeeper requested a great hall inspection at eighteen today, and the secretary confirmed a meeting with the builder at the hall entrance at seventeen fifty-five. I do not yet know why the inspection was requested or what preparations are for. I have returned from tea for office hours and asked the secretary whether any business or correspondence has arrived. My next concrete commitment is the builder meeting and hall inspection. For now, uncertainty and rumours are the unusual features of the day, not a verified secret undertaking.
